strengths: Strong cold open, a clear risk-transfer thesis, and a rare fair presentation of the counter-argument.
Source-conflict handling (New York Fed vs advocacy group) and average-versus-median demonstrations.
Echo ending that returns to the mail.
weaknesses: Action section is thin relative to the problem.
Title and thumbnail promise a wipe-out the script rejects.
A 45% access claim conflicts with BLS; the "one month in 11" scaling is wrong.
Envelope numbers skip without explanation and the "most damage" ranking is not shown.
contradictions: "About to get wiped out" versus "isn't being wiped out by a crash".
"Like and subscribe" at ~1,160 characters versus the rule-of-value-first.
Juny "who had just graduated" in the opening versus "graduated this spring" later.
improvement_opportunities: Retitle toward the thesis: "Why Your Raise Disappears: The Risk Transfer Nobody Priced In".
Put the actual letter (an escrow analysis) in the thumbnail instead of the broken piggy bank, to match the opening.
Replace "45% have access" with the BLS 72% private and 44% part-time split.
Show Marisol's raise as a table: +$240 a month, -$84 escrow, premium, deductible, groceries, so the "poorer by March" claim is audited on screen.
Move the like/subscribe ask after the first envelope payoff and expand the two actions with a worked example for Juny.
unavailable: Primary KFF, Vanguard, AEI, Brookings, Harvard JCHS documents
